summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would remove the maximum rates set in the Primary Industries (Customs) Charges Act 1999 for research and development and marketing charges.
It would allow the government to set new charge rates through regulations alone, without needing to amend the Act, and would require the Minister to consult industry bodies before setting rates.
The bill would also prevent regulations from setting a charge rate above what the relevant industry body recommends, which the government says safeguards against excessive increases.
changes: Removes product-specific maximum rates for research and development and marketing charges from the Act.
Allows charge rates to be changed by amending regulations only, not the Act.
Strengthens consultation requirements so the Minister must consider industry body recommendations.
Restricts regulations from setting a rate higher than the industry body's recommended rate.
summary.affected: Primary producers and industry bodies that pay or propose research and development and marketing charges, and the 15 rural research and development corporations.

speeches.speaker: Barnaby Joyce
speeches.brief: Moved the Primary Industries (Excise) Levies Amendment Bill 2013, which removes the legislated maximum rate for research, development and marketing levies and requires new rates to be recommended by industry bodies in consultation with levy payers, implementing a 2011 Productivity Commission recommendation.

speeches.speaker: Philip Ruddock
speeches.brief: Referred the Rural Research and Development Legislation Amendment Bill 2013, the Primary Industries (Excise) Levies Amendment Bill 2013 and the Primary Industries (Customs) Charges Amendment Bill 2013 to the Federation Chamber for further consideration.

speeches.speaker: Jill Hall
speeches.brief: Supported the Rural Research and Development Legislation Amendment Bill 2013 and companion levy bills amending 10 acts, noting they were first introduced on 19 June before lapsing when the election was called, and welcomed extending marketing activities and matched funding to statutory research and development corporations.

speeches.speaker: Julie Owens
speeches.brief: Argued that the bill builds on the research and development corporation model established in 1989 under the Hawke government, and that it lets statutory bodies undertake marketing, extends government matching of voluntary contributions, removes the requirement to submit annual operating plans for ministerial approval, and allows individual fishery sectors to set their own levies.

speeches.speaker: Sharman Stone
speeches.brief: Supported the bill's marketing provisions for statutory research and development corporations, but argued that the Coles and Woolworths duopoly discourages food innovation by quickly copying successful branded products as cheaper home-brand versions, citing Heinz's departure from regional Victoria as a result.

speeches.speaker: Stephen Jones
speeches.brief: Supported the rural research and development bills, noting a similar bill was introduced on 19 June in the 43rd Parliament but lapsed when parliament was prorogued in August, and welcomed provisions letting statutory bodies market their industries and matching voluntary research contributions without changing existing levy rates.

speeches.speaker: Kevin Hogan
speeches.brief: Supported the bill's marketing provisions, noting that only 22 per cent of prawns sold in New South Wales are caught locally, and that the electorate's macadamia growers invest more than $4 million a year in research and development to keep pace with export demand.

speeches.speaker: Tony Zappia
speeches.brief: Welcomed extending industry-specific levies to fisheries under the National Food Plan, and warned that Australia's spending on rural research and development has fallen from ninth to 16th internationally since 2000, threatening future farm productivity growth.

speeches.speaker: Mark Coulton
speeches.brief: Supported the Primary Industries (Customs) Charges Amendment Bill 2013 and related legislation, noting the government will provide around $250 million to rural research and development corporations this financial year plus an additional $100 million from next year, and defended family farms against comments from the Australian Workers Union that farming should be corporatised.

speeches.speaker: Rowan Ramsey
speeches.brief: Supported the Rural Research and Development Legislation Amendment Bill 2013 and related bills, describing how Grains Research and Development Corporation levies of about $2.50 per tonne generate roughly $80 million a year, to be matched at an increased rate of $1.25 for every industry dollar under the coalition's election commitment.
